- Overestimate prices during sentiment spikes (especially when sentiment > 0.5) — reduce forecast by 1–3% for high sentiment days.
- Underestimate during prolonged negative sentiment (sentiment < 0.3) — add 1–2% to forecast to account for mean reversion or policy-driven support.
- Overshoot after sharp price spikes — cap forecast at 10–15% below peak if sentiment turns neutral or negative.
- Lagged price movements: if 3–5 day history shows upward trend, forecast should not exceed 2–3% above recent high unless sentiment confirms continuation.
- Mean reversion bias: if 10+ days of price consolidation, forecast should be closer to 30-day moving average than to recent peak.
- Sentiment-driven volatility: if sentiment > 0.6, allow 2–3% higher forecast volatility; if < 0.4, reduce volatility by 1–2% to avoid overcorrection.
